The Unreal Past: Present Results of a Past Condition
You can use conditional sentences to talk about two different times. These sentences are called "mixed conditionals" and are formed differently from the zero, first, second and third conditional.

The first type of mixed conditional refers to a condition in the past and a result in the present that is the opposite of what really happened. You need to remember the truth of the situation so that you can use the affirmative or negative of the verb accordingly to make the opposite in the conditional sentence.

Grammar structure:
if + past perfect, would + base form of the verb
would + base form of the verb... if + past perfect

Compare the mixed conditional with the 3rd conditional that you learnt before:
If I had gone to the doctor, I would have gotten a prescription for some medicine. (3rd conditional = unreal in the past)
The truth is that I didn't go to the doctor, and I didn't get a prescription for some medicine (in the past).

If I had gone to the doctor, I would feel better now. (mixed conditional = unreal in the past and unreal present result)
The truth is that I didn't go to the doctor (in the past) and I don't feel better now (in the present).
You can place the if-clause after the main clause as well. If you do, you don't need to use commas after it.

If you had asked for directions, we wouldn't be lost right now.
We wouldn't be lost right now if you had asked for directions.
In both sentences above, the true situation is that you didn't ask for directions and that we are lost now.
You know if Sally hadn't left so suddenly, I wouldn't be feeling this way.
If I had stayed home tonight, I would be feeling so jealous right now.
If I had had more time along the way, I would be taking singing lessons.
If I had worked less, I would be doing more cool stuff.
If he had been single, I would marry him in an instant.
Time Clauses: Talking about the Past
You can use different time expressions like before, after and as soon as, in time clauses to talk about events in the past.
In speaking, it is common for you to use the simple past in both the time clause and the main clause. The order of events is clear because of the meaning of the conjunction itself.

Examples:
Before I wrote my exam, I studied with my friends at the library. (I studied with friends, and then I wrote my exam.)
After I wrote my final exam, my friends and I went out to celebrate. (I wrote my exam, and then my friends and I went out to celebrate.)
I called my mother as soon as I found out my exam results. (I found out my exam results first and then called my mother.)

The use of when with both events in the simple past also tells you the order of events, with the time clause event happening first.
Example:
When I got home, I took a shower. (I got home first and then took a shower.)
If you want to emphasize that one action happened and finished before another, you can use the past perfect verb tense (had + past participle). This will show the first action that happened.

Example:
After I had washed my car, it started to rain.
As soon as I had fallen asleep, the phone rang.
I had already left the party before my friends arrived.

images.text:
Vanessa: Peter. Come in. What's up?
Peter: I don't know. I wanted to ask you a couple of questions.
Vanessa: Oh yeah. What's that?
Peter: Have you ever wondered what it is like to be a rock and roll star?
Vanessa: Sure, my friends and I always pretended to be singers when we were children. As I got older, I pretended to be Mariah Carey. Once, my friends and I even dressed up as KISS. You know, if I had more time along the way, I would be taking singing lessons.
Peter: Have you ever considered who the best band in the world is right now?

Vanessa: We talked about that last night while we were eating dinner. We said the Foo Fighters.
Peter: The Foo Fighters! That is correct!
Vanessa: Peter! What have you done?
Peter: Here.
Vanessa: Two tickets to Foo Fighters and are these backstage passes? Peter!
Peter: Concert starts in an hour. As soon as you're ready, we can go. Shake a leg!
Vanessa: This is so exciting!

(Three hours later in a pub downtown.)

Vanessa: What a fantastic concert. I had the time of my life. If I had stayed home tonight, I would be feeling so jealous right now.
Peter: Haha. Had you been backstage at a concert before tonight?
Vanessa: No! Well. I had been backstage for amateur nights at pubs in England.
Peter: I bet you had never met the lead singer of a famous rock band before tonight either?
Vanessa: I can't believe I met Dave Grohl. He was so cordial and amiable and so ... nice.
Peter: Really? I found him to be stuck up and pompous.
Vanessa: If he had been single, I would marry him in an instant. Like that. Oh, Peter. If I had worked less, I would be doing more cool stuff. I guess I've been too busy dealing with work. Peter, before tonight, I was feeling really low. You know if Sally hadn't left so suddenly I wouldn't be feeling this way.
Peter: Yeah. Listen, V. I really miss Sally too. I know we can talk to her online anytime we want, but it's different. It's that whole out of sight out of mind thing. I want to let you know, I am always here for you.
Vanessa: That is the sweetest thing anyone has ever said to me. You're a good friend.
Peter: So are you. The best!
